module purpose: Top-level NEORV32 CPU entity that wires together the frontend, control, regfile, ALU, LSU, PMP, counters and optional ICC. It forwards clock/reset and interrupt inputs to subunits, accepts fetched instructions from the frontend, receives sub-unit results (ALU, LSU, CSR, counters, PMP, ICC), and produces control signals (ctrl) that direct execution and route writeback data to the regfile.

use-case flows.value: instruction fetch delivered from frontend to control (fetched instruction + valid fields)
control generation and distribution: control core computes the ctrl record and drives it to execution subunits
ALU computation and delivery of ALU result into the writeback mux (alu_res -> rf_wdata)
Load-store return: LSU produces load data (lsu_rdata) which feeds the writeback mux
Register-file read/write: regfile provides rs1/rs2/rs3 to execution units and accepts rf_wdata as rd (writeback)
CSR read aggregation: xcsr_res collects CSR sources (counters, ALU, PMP, ICC) and is delivered into control as xcsr_rdata_i
machine-interrupt combination: mti_i, mei_i and msi_i are combined into irq_machine and passed to control
reset (rstn_i) is forwarded into instantiated sub-units (they are reset by rstn_i)

conceptual assets.concept: Control decisions produced by the control core (the 'ctrl' record) that direct ALU/LSU/regfile/CSR/PMP/ICC behaviour
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control instance neorv32_cpu_control_inst drives the top-level ctrl record (port map ctrl_o => ctrl; RTL port-map lines around 205..253) and that record is consumed by multiple execution subunits (regfile, ALU, LSU, PMP, ICC; port-map lines 321,362,384,414,441..444). The relationship map shows ctrl is delivered by the control instance (ctrl occurrence 3, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_control_inst.ctrl_o at RTL line 253) and thus the module guarantees that the consumers receive exactly the ctrl value the control core produces; corrupting ctrl would violate operation integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: Fetched instruction stream (frontend outputs) delivered into the control pipeline
conceptual assets.reasoning: The frontend instance produces the frontend record (port map frontend_o => frontend at RTL line 199) and the control instance reads it (frontend_i => frontend at RTL line 255). The map records the production (frontend occurrence 2, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_frontend_inst.frontend_o at line 199) and the consumer connection, so the integrity of the fetched-instruction value that the control decodes is established by these connections.

conceptual assets.concept: Register write-back data (rf_wdata) selected from ALU / LSU / CSR / pc_ret and presented to the regfile for rd
conceptual assets.reasoning: The top-level assignment rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret (RTL line 330) implements the writeback selection; the regfile receives this value through its rd_i port (port map rd_i => rf_wdata at RTL line 323). The map records rf_wdata as derived from alu_res, csr_rdata, ctrl.pc_ret and lsu_rdata (rf_wdata occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM at line 330 targeting those signals) and the connection into the regfile (occurrence 2, connection at line 323). Thus the integrity of the writeback value delivered to the regfile is established by these RTL connections.

conceptual assets.concept: ALU result produced by the ALU and consumed by writeback and other logic (alu_res)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The ALU instance drives the top-level alu_res (neorv32_cpu_alu_inst res_o => alu_res at RTL line 369) and rf_wdata uses alu_res as one writeback source (rf_wdata line 330). The map shows the ALU delivers this value (alu_res occurrence 3, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_alu_inst.res_o at line 369) and that rf_wdata derives from it (rf_wdata DERIVES_FROM target alu_res at line 330). Therefore the integrity of ALU results as delivered to the writeback path is established by the RTL wiring.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file read operands (rs1, rs2) provided by the regfile to execution units
conceptual assets.reasoning: The regfile instance exports rs1/rs2 and execution units consume them (regfile rs1_o/rs2_o => rs1/rs2 at RTL lines 324..325; ALU and LSU take these signals at lines 364..365 and 387). The map shows rs1 and rs2 are driven by the regfile outputs (rs1 occurrence 3, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst.rs1_o at line 324; rs2 occurrence 2, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst.rs2_o at line 325) and are read by ALU/LSU, so the integrity of operands used for computation is established by these connections.

conceptual assets.concept: Combined machine-interrupt signal (irq_machine) computed from external interrupt inputs and delivered to control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The top-level combines interrupt inputs (RTL line 276: irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i) and forwards the result into the control instance (port map irq_machine_i => irq_machine at RTL line 267). The map records the combinational derivation (irq_machine occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM at line 276 targeting mei_i, msi_i, mti_i) and the connection into control (occurrence 2, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_control_inst.irq_machine_i at line 267). The control decisions therefore depend on the exact irq_machine value produced here, establishing its integrity as a primary asset; the external inputs that set it are shown by the map (e.g., msi_i occurrence 2, SOURCES partner irq_machine at line 276).

conceptual assets.concept: Aggregated CSR read value (xcsr_res) formed from counters/ALU/PMP/ICC and presented to control as xcsr_rdata_i
conceptual assets.reasoning: xcsr_res is formed by OR'ing multiple sub-unit CSR sources in the top-level (RTL line 279: xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc) and is fed into the control instance as xcsr_rdata_i (port map line 264). The map shows xcsr_res derives from those xcsr_* signals (xcsr_res occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM at line 279 targeting xcsr_cnt,xcsr_alu,xcsr_pmp,xcsr_icc) and that at least the counters supply xcsr_cnt (xcsr_cnt connection at occurrence 3, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_counters_inst.rdata_o at line 299). Control sees this aggregated value, so its integrity is established by the RTL wiring.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP fault indicator (pmp_fault) produced by PMP and consumed by control/LSU
conceptual assets.reasoning: When PMP is enabled the PMP unit drives a fault signal (neorv32_cpu_pmp_inst.fault_o => pmp_fault at RTL line 420) and that signal is consumed by control and the LSU (port maps at lines 257 and 392). The map shows pmp_fault driven by the PMP instance (pmp_fault occurrence 4, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_pmp_inst.fault_o at line 420) and also shows a conditional constant driver when PMP is disabled (constant driver at occurrence 5, value '0' under configuration not RISCV_ISA_Smpmp at line 427). The PMP fault's integrity (and its conditional presence) is therefore established by the RTL wiring and configuration.

conceptual assets.concept: Load data returned by the LSU (lsu_rdata) that feeds writeback
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU instance provides load data on rdata_o which is wired into the top-level lsu_rdata signal (port map rdata_o => lsu_rdata at RTL line 388); rf_wdata derives from lsu_rdata (rf_wdata assignment at line 330). The map records this (lsu_rdata occurrence 3, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_lsu_inst.rdata_o at line 388 and rf_wdata DERIVES_FROM lsu_rdata at line 330), establishing the integrity of loaded data as delivered for writeback.

conceptual assets.concept: CSR read data produced by the control core (csr_rdata) that can be written back to registers
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control instance outputs csr_rdata (port map csr_rdata_o => csr_rdata at RTL line 263) and rf_wdata derives from csr_rdata (rf_wdata <= ... csr_rdata ... at line 330). The map shows csr_rdata produced by the control instance (csr_rdata occurrence 2, CONNECTS partner neorv32_cpu_control_inst.csr_rdata_o at line 263) and used as a writeback source (rf_wdata DERIVES_FROM csr_rdata at line 330), so the integrity of CSR read results produced by control is established by the RTL wiring.
